interview_log.question: Problem & goals — What's the core problem today, and what does success look like if this is solved?
interview_log.answer: Traditional CRMs fail because logging a meeting means stopping to fill forms — a disconnected step reps skip or delay, so data quality suffers and adoption stays low. Commitments made in conversation live only in memory or inboxes, with no system tracking follow-through, and reconstructing "where things stand" with a customer means manually piecing together notes and emails. Success means capture becomes as effortless as sending a text, so it happens every time. Commitments get tracked automatically and surfaced before they're due, and relationship history becomes instantly queryable instead of archaeological. The result: reps actually use it because it removes work rather than adds it, and relationship knowledge lives in a shared system, not individual heads.

interview_log.question: Primary users — Who is this mainly for? What do they need in order to use it at all?
interview_log.answer: sales rep, and for prerquisite we will be having seeded data

interview_log.question: Follow-up: do reps need to log in individually (so commitments/notes are attributed to a specific person), or is a single shared login enough for the demo, given it is a web app used on presumably a laptop/desktop after a meeting?
interview_log.answer: single shared login for the demo

interview_log.question: Other participants — Is there a second group with different needs, or is it genuinely single-audience?
interview_log.answer: same role sharing the same capabilities

interview_log.question: Current pain points — What do people do today instead, and what is wrong with it?
interview_log.answer: not sure what people use these days, we are building a demo based on what we know and have shared

interview_log.question: Scope boundaries — What is explicitly out of scope for this first version?
interview_log.answer: for the demo we are not focusing on any real integrations, and no multi team and multi tenant support. There won't be any real system integrations. We'll use adapters to simulate the external connections.

interview_log.question: Constraints & integrations — Any existing systems, data sources, platform requirements or policies this has to work within?
interview_log.answer: we will be using seeded data for the demo purposes, seeded data will have MOM, emails, sharepoint.

interview_log.question: Success metrics — How would we know, concretely, that this worked?
interview_log.answer: agents functioning end to end on the seeded data.

interview_log.question: Risks & compliance — Anything sensitive here — personal data, money, safety, regulation — that needs care?
interview_log.answer: seeded data only no real data for now

findings.finding: roles/discovery.json has no `artifacts` array (and no `version` field). `tools/record-validation.cjs` builds the gate manifest strictly from `s.artifacts`, and refuses to record any review when that array is empty or absent ("the role records no artifacts, so there is nothing for the gate manifest to pin"). As currently written, `./sparc.sh record-validation workflow-1-discovery-to-stories discovery <findings.json>` will exit with an error and record nothing -- this review would never actually land in state.
findings.evidence: roles/discovery.json holds only `discovery.brief_document` as a bare string path; there is no top-level `version` or `artifacts` field anywhere in the file. record-validation.cjs lines ~121-137: `const artifacts = s.artifacts ?? []; ... if (!manifest.length) die('the role records no artifacts, so there is nothing for the gate manifest to pin. A validation of no artifact is not evidence.');`. discovery-agent.md's Output section (lines ~101-107) never instructs the agent to write a `version` or `artifacts` field, only `discovery.brief_document`.
findings.suggested_fix: Before running record-validation, add to roles/discovery.json: `"version": "1.0"` and `"artifacts": [{ "role": "discovery", "path": "docs/discovery/DISCOVERY-BRIEF-conversational-crm-v1.0.md", "version": "1.0" }]`. Longer term, discovery-agent.md's Output section should be updated to always write these two fields, the same way workflow-2/3 role files already do, so this does not recur on every future run of workflow 1.

findings.finding: The Discovery Brief omits every specific named agent and concrete capability described in the original seed idea (`project.idea_input`): the Capture Agent, Extraction Agent, Memory/Q&A Agent, Commitment Tracking Agent, and Brief-Me-on-Customer Agent are never mentioned, nor are business-card scanning, natural-language query examples ("what did we discuss last time?"), the due-soon/overdue commitment list, the customer profile view, the shared view for a second team member, or optional voice-note capture. `discovery.interview_log`'s answers already paraphrase these away into generic language ("capture becomes effortless", "commitments get tracked automatically"), and the Brief -- correctly, given its own rule of only using the transcript -- inherited that genericness. Because Requirements/PRD is instructed to build strictly from this Brief (not from `idea_input` directly), there is a real risk that the concrete, differentiating product capabilities named in the original idea never resurface as PRD features.
findings.evidence: workflow.json `project.idea_input` names five specific agents and several concrete UX flows in detail. None of these terms or flows appear anywhere in DISCOVERY-BRIEF-conversational-crm-v1.0.md, whose Goals section is generic paraphrase. discovery-agent.md's Startup step 3 instructs the agent to read only `discovery.interview_log` and `discovery.open_items`, not `project.idea_input`, so nothing in the process re-checks the Brief against the original idea.
findings.suggested_fix: Before Requirements drafts the PRD, have a human confirm at the discovery gate whether these specific agents/capabilities are still intended for this build. If so, either run one more interview round to surface them explicitly (so they enter `interview_log` and can be added to the Brief without violating its own no-new-facts rule), or explicitly note in the Brief's Open Items that `project.idea_input` contains product specifics not yet reconciled with the interview transcript.

findings.suggested_fix: Add the `[INFERRED — needs confirmation]` tag to the Section 5 sentence, or fold it into the existing Section 2 inference so the same underlying inference isn't stated once as fact and once as a flagged assumption.
